notes.claim: A lead-acid cell is nominally 2 V, and a charged, rested cell reads about 2.1 V open circuit.
Cells connect in series to make a battery: six 2 V cells make a 12 V battery.

sources.title: 17.5 Batteries and Fuel Cells - Chemistry 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: Each cell produces 2 V, so six cells are connected in series to produce a 12-V car battery.

sources.title: Battery University | BU-303: Confusion with Voltages
sources.quote: The nominal voltage of lead acid is 2 volts per cell, however when measuring the open circuit voltage, the OCV of a charged and rested battery should be 2.1V/cell.
